newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - UK, German stocks end down on new rate fears.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - UK, German stocks end down on new rate fears.

text.p: Key European bourses ended down after touching peaks on Tuesday as worries about U.S. interest rates were rekindled, ending Wall Street's record-breaking run.

London and Frankurt soared briefly to new highs, cheered by a short-lived positive opening on Wall Street, then quickly lost ground as the tide in New York changed and stocks plunged 0.6 percent in the first hour.
Wall Street's early gains were wiped out after comments by a senior central bank Federal Reserve official led the market to believe interest rates might be raised.

The unidentified official told Reuters eight out of 12 Fed banks had asked for an increase in the five percent discount rate. Of the eight banks, three had requested a raise in interest rates of 50 basis points.

"There's no question that the comments brought down bonds and stocks. The stock market started going down...right after the news came over" said Peter Canelo, chief investment strategist at Dean Witter in New York.
The change in mood came after London and Frankfurt had both opened strongly, powered by Monday's record close on Wall Street where hopes had grown that U.S. interest rates would remain unchanged.

But the European gains were fragile even though Monday's stampede on Wall Street had driven London's FTSE 100 index to a trading peak of 3,986.7 points. By mid-afternoon, the jitters had set in and London closed down 4.9 points.
"We had the ingredients this morning of approaching and maybe even breaching 4,000 but there is and continues to be reluctance to do that," said one senior trader.
"The demand is just not there. The buyers are a bit reluctant to commit themselves at the higher levels. The sellers don't want to sell anyway," he said.
The European markets ran out of steam as doubts took hold about the durability of Wall Street's run and the fresh doubts arose about interest rates in the influential American economy.

Frankfurt ended in negative territory after touching a new high in opening deals on the computerised IBIS index. Floor trading ended down 1.79 points on the DAX index after closing at a record high of 2,629.87 on Monday.
French shares also closed lower, reversing their gains in late trade because of worries over U.S. interest rates.

The dollar was higher at the end of European trade, buoyed by the Fed official's comments. Any increase in U.S. interest rates would tend to make the dollar more attractive to foreign exchange dealers.
The dollar was also helped by higher-than-expected U.S. industrial production figures for August.
"It's a combination of dollar-positive elements that allowed the dollar to go higher, such as the Fed comments and the latest data," said Tim Fox, treasury economist at Standard Chartered.
Despite intraday gains of half a pfennig, the dollar ran into stiff resistance at 1.5160, a technical level broken briefly last Friday but still in place as a major barrier.
"We need a convincing break of that level but it's difficult because there's an awful lot of offers in that area," said a trader at a U.S. bank.
CURRENCIES
The dollar was at 1.5150 marks and 110.37 yen in late European markets, compared with Monday's 1.5105 marks and 110.13 yen.
STOCK MARKETS
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares ended 4.9 points lower at 3,972.3.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index finished down 5.33 at 2,080.86.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed down 1.79 at 2,628.08.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed at $383.55, compared with $382.70 at the London close on Monday. Silver ended at $5.07, up two cents.
